After TF2, nobody has figured out how to make an arena FPS that normies will play, and the armchair game devs who always pretend like they know how to make it work don't actually know either. GD Studio is taking another stab at that gargantuan task by trying something new and putting in the effort.

TL;DR: This is a good game with an unfairly low rating because some Quake players are butthurt that this isn't Quake Champions 2. Negative reviews are overwhelmingly from Quake and original Diabotical players. Go figure. For those of you who missed the launch of the original Diabotical, it was supposed to be the successor to Quake. It had a great early access run then a solid first few months after launch before it tanked. While it was populated, it was amazing, but arena shooters are difficult to get into. Lots of weapons and unique movement mechanics which a lot of players find very difficult to master. Diabotical was no different in that regard, but it had a practice arena for learning the game which was very useful. I used it a ton. I was a new AFPS player and stuck through getting destroyed for awhile. I put a lot of hours into becoming a decent player only to have the game die right after. The Quake players absolutely demolished the new players, which led to them not coming back. The devs were really open to feedback, and unfortunately, a lot of that feedback was from Quake players who often weren't open to things that weren't exactly like Quake. The AFPS community has some snobs, and that type of person wants this game to follow the same failure of a formula that DBT did. The main casual mode in DBT, Wipeout, for example, was whined about on a regular basis because it had a comeback mechanic. It was just a little bit friendly to newer players, and many Quake players wouldn't have it. You may even see reviews of this game with those complaints if you look. I loved that game mode, and I'm happy to see it return. Strafe jumping, which was a substantial barrier to entry, has thankfully been removed. This is beneficial to new players, but the snobby side of the AFPS community can't stand it. Cry me a river. The game is good. A bit heavy on the rogue elements for my taste, but good. Go ruin someone else's good time, parasites. Every negative review of this game from an AFPS snob is an advertisement. What's bad for them is good for you. Edit 1: There have been numerous small updates and bug fixes in the few days since early access started. RNG has been toned down a bit with players now choosing their bot's ability, which no longer changes between rounds once selected. Currency earnings have been lowered, which means fewer upgrades. The currency system went overboard before IMO, so this change is great, too. Sliding got a necessary buff. Teams get reroll tokens for upgrades after a round loss. Devs have been quick to respond to feedback, and the game is already trending in a good direction. Fingers crossed for more updates that help inexperienced players. Edit 2: Raven is still killing it with the updates. Slide-hopping is awesome now. Balancing is getting better. The biggest complaint I have right now is that Scout is a little OP. Easily the most popular class. People are still playing other classes often, but every now and then you might run into a team with 3 or 4 Scouts. Scout has the most powerful weapon, the most powerful movement ability, the most narrow physical build, and the ability to heal itself and teammates. With that said, it's still not OP to the point where you have to use it. Scout-heavy teams seem to win more often so far in my experience.

The original diabotical was a really good game in my opinion. This one feels like a different team was tasked to make diabotical with rng and classes. I don't generally mind classes, but the combination we have at hand doesn't work too well I'd argue. In this game you play 4x4 bo7 matches, with your weapons and secondary ability randomised with each round. That means, the game is extremely RNG, and right now, with how poor the balancing is, getting worse weapons could literally lose you a round. To add insult to injury, this issue is being greatly alleviated by RNG roguelike element: After each round(or sometimes during the game when met certain conditions) you get to choose 1 card out of 3 random ones, which costs some "points" you earn during the round. You can get upgrades for your character which are always the same, but they're generally weak. The strongest upgrades are for the guns and secondary ability, and that's a problem. You can get a couple of good upgrades for a good gun and have a great round to not get this gun ever again during this round. There's also an another separate permanent upgrade system which I'm not a huge fan of. It does give you some nice things, even if they don't feel extremely overpowered. So, in general it's a boring team wipeout mode game with classes, no interesting movement (not even strafe jumps?), based completely around RNG. If you don't think that sounds fun, it's because it is not. P.S: I like the maps, and the lobby is really cool. Pickups that spawn on the ground and you have to stand on top of them to "capture" them is also a mechanic I like. Maybe this game would be worth to check in half a year, but with how diabotical went, I don't have high hopes for this one, I'm sorry.

Reading some other reviews, I have to say: hating on developers for not flushing hundreds of thousands of dollars down the toilet by developing the next old school afps trying to revive the genre is exactly what I would expect from the veteran afps community. After having Quake Live, Reflex Arena, Toxic, Diabotical, tons of other smaller games and Quake Champions (somewhat) flop, they still have not understood that the problem which each of those games dying in less than 3 months are not the developers but the players whose interest has simply shifted. I don't like modern shooters either, but simply accepting that the 90s are over would reduce the toxicity around these games a lot. GD Studio have understood this and are now bombarded with hate for trying to bring both "genres" together - how dare they, I guess... About the actual game - it's fun and it has a few neat ideas that we haven't seen before in the modern multiplayer space. If you like afps games of pretty much any kind and you like other games that are not Quake Live, you'll have fun playing this.

Pros - I quite like the lobby system - There are lots of options to change your setup if you are interested in that Cons - There is very little communication to a new player as to what to expect when you are entering a multi player match - Every time you select a class, the weapons you have are randomised - The cards are not explained well, you get currency each round of play which lets you pick cards that change your characters performance... but it doesnt say you can reroll, and I dont understand what some of it does (sometimes it applies to weapons you might not get) - A lot popping up cards and information regularly which is confusing and disruptive - Maps are too small for the existing mode - The community is quite small at the moment, each of the 3 games I played were a steamroll one way or another. Usually with at least 1 player on a side who has significantly more experience with the game compared to others. This game doesn't really know what it's trying to be. It's got some interesting concepts but they are all mashed together. It's far too random to be appealing for casual players (like myself), and also not at all intuitive to get the hang of quickly. If they had larger maps and more objective-based modes then it could be more interesting. But at the moment it is really missing a hook. Interviews with James Harding, the CEO and Lead Designer, suggest that they are getting regular feedback from pro esports players of different games. However, the team needs to get some feedback from the type of players which they want to attract. Let's face it, professional gamers are a significant minority of any game's player base. I will potentially try this again if the game is revamped a bit - currently quite disappointing.

Can't really recommend this. The balance is pretty whack, and this is amplified by it being random weapons and buffs. There are also a fair amount of upgrades that are locked entirely behind long term progression, which is capped weekly for some reason. The movement can sometimes feel satisfying, but being fast is all about a mostly unfun slidehop. Also, the sniper class is insane. I don't know who thought it was a good idea to give an aoe heal tool to the class with the highest single target DPS, but here we are. It's also pretty insane that the zoom on weapons is its own FOV slider, which applies to ALL guns. Want a sniper to zoom more than all the other guns? Not possible. The roguelite elements only take away from this game, in my opinion. Would have been more satisfying with just loadouts and regular balance, instead of the one-off chance that you MIGHT get a godgun. The game also expects you to switch off a class if the guns aren't great, but then you've invested upgrades into a class, so switching is often a bad choice too. I don't think any FPS should have a system that makes it so you can't pick your guns. Pretty insane design choice. This game will die as quickly as it appeared, never breaking 300 players. It's just kind of a shame, the game LOOKS fun when you see people play it, and it does have its moments. And then you spawn and get instantly headshot and die right away, and sometimes will have to wait over 30 seconds before you can play again. I forgot to talk about the absolutely insane gamemode of Wipeout. You have to full clear the enemy team with the respawn timers getting longer and longer. The mode encourages literally hiding for your team to re spawn. It's also the ONLY MODE in the game, unless you count the warmup. I don't. Altogether, can't recommend this if you are an OG quake fan. Can't recommend it if you like ability based shooters. I don't know who this game is for, but probably the tiny player base who you will get in every match. Sometimes it even struggles to fill 4v4 lobbies lmaoo. Edit: Tried to play more and they did something to this game where it just can't run well anymore. Can barely break 30 fps when I was steadily getting over 120 before. Literally unplayable and lobbies won't fill at primetime. Don't buy this.

Edit/Update: as of 12/22/24 this project, which was introduced as a multiplayer title, appears to be virtually dead. The studio, as far as I can tell, is attempting to turn DBTR into single-player game, something nobody wanted. Do with that info as you will, and feel free to disregard the original positive review I posted below. I've become a full-blown AFPS addict over the past decade, logging thousands of hours in games like Quake Live. I've also dabbled heavily in more modern fare, stuff like Overwatch and Apex Legends. I've enjoyed these newer games well enough but always find myself returning to my beloved boomer shooters where individual skill expression reigns supreme. The problems of the arena shooter are well-known: they are annoyingly, prohibitively difficult, and require that players invest massive amounts of time to reach baseline levels of competence. They are games that are straitjacketed by their own purity and hardcoreness. They lack wide appeal. But they are arguably the pinnacle of the FPS genre. On the other side exist comparatively shallow modern FPS games, which provide fun and reward without much commitment. These are games that don’t want for players, but they often attract their huge playerbases by sacrificing depth, interesting mechanics, and in many instances, particularly for the competitive player, fairness and competitive balance. Given this reality, I’m always on the lookout for that unicorn game, the one that can successfully bridge these worlds, something that is both fun and modern without sacrificing the nuance and challenge that I’ve grown to appreciate, and expect, during my time in Quake. It is hard for me to see DBTR as anything other than an attempt to be one of these unicorn games. And to be blunt: I do not think that DBTR succeeds in doing this. But I think it eventually might, given more time. DBTR, in my opinion, is more demo than game at this point. I’d say that the game is around 5, maybe 10, percent complete. Still, what does exist is quite good, and the tempo of the combat feels fast and fluid, despite removing standard strafe jumping mechanics. However, in my view, the biggest argument for supporting the game is the studio itself. For whatever reason, the GD studio is unusually responsive to player feedback, and they regularly incorporate community suggestions into game patches. This means that players can play a noticeable role in shaping the game. This is obviously a double-edged sword, as it only works well if discerning devs can sort good ideas from bad. It also depends for its effectiveness on a community that comes up with useful ideas and gives constructive feedback. But it does present a cool opportunity to contribute to a game in development. As a player, your feedback will be seen, considered, and potentially even implemented by the developers if you are active in the game's communication channels (discord, reddit, etc.), and I think that alone is worth the price of admission, if you are an FPS fan. There are only two groups of players I would urge to avoid this game. First, if you are looking for a game that is fully formed—not just in its gameplay loop but in terms of its larger conception—I would give this game a pass. This game is clearly still trying to find its exact identity. I would also avoid this game if you are a hardcore, competitive AFPS player who simply wants another q3 rehash or, on the other end, count yourself among the most casual, aim-assisted weekend warriors. Members of the first group will find DBTR, at least in current form, too easy and the movement too neutered to be interesting. Members of the second group will find the game too challenging. But I think those in the middle 95% (or outliers in the tails, who have open minds) will find it worthwhile.

So unfortunately this game is dead right now. Maybe somewhere out there is an active server, but not anywhere in the U.S. This is honestly a neat game, but it's a cutthroat market out there for multiplayer and this game was brutal. It reminded me a lot of Quake Live in that you lose to the person using the railgun every time. You lived and died by skillshots with snipers and the sniper equivalents. There was no need for the other weapons, they were just outclassed 100%. In its last days, it was only people doing skillshots, but at its healthiest every match was dominated by someone who couldn't be stopped using the sniper or its equivalent. In a roguelite with all of these perks, metaprogression, and abilities, it really killed any interest in engaging with the unique elements of the game. Again, cutthroat market, and this game was not balanced well enough to maintain an audience even though it was well made. Maybe it'll bounce back though. This game would have been cool if you could reasonably use more than one type of weapon.

I don't understand how this game hasn't gained more traction. The base movement is super fluid and creative, gunplay is great, variety of guns is perfect, maps are solid, the game runs smooth, clip-worthy gameplay, and there's even a big pre-game lobby where you can roam around and test every gun/ability. I understand the card system to choose guns/abilities isn't for everyone but it's well-done and keeps the game fresh and fun between each match. This is the perfect arena shooter imo. If it had even a little bit of a playerbase I'd easily have a couple hundred hours logged. Hopeful this game eventually gets the attention it deserves. A+

I get that it's Early Access but the devs need to be better with communicating whether they're still working on this or not. This has been a recurring problem with this company where you'd only know about things happening if you happen to tune into long impromptu Twitch streams announced with very little advance notice on Reddit or Discord and are left completely in the dark otherwise. The community that already plays the original Diabotical never liked this game's concept to begin with and would rather have the original game on Steam instead which leaves Rogue in the unfortunate position of trying to please everybody and pleasing nobody in the process. There's hints that the devs have been working on PvE or MOBA style modes for several months but as of right now it's impossible to play this game with other people unless you're involved in the Discord community and get PUGs in whatever modes other people feel like playing. Even then the Discord is mostly just DBT 1 sh*tposters who spam the :smileyblue: emoji because they don't actually like playing DBT Rogue to begin with. There are already weapon skins in this game that you can't get because they were exclusive Twitch drops from last year, which kind of tells you where the devs' priorities are. At this rate we're on track to see Battlebit Remastered get an update before this game gets anything again.
